subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: moves DC power either way between car battery and grid.

subsystems.name: Onboard battery and management
subsystems.role: supplies the energy; must accept extra cycles without undue wear.

subsystems.name: Communication and control protocol
subsystems.role: lets car and charger agree on power, timing and safety.

subsystems.name: Aggregation platform
subsystems.role: bundles hundreds or thousands of parked cars into one controllable block.

subsystems.name: Grid interface
subsystems.role: connects the aggregated fleet to the distribution network legally and safely.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and settlement
subsystems.role: tracks energy and payments and protects batteries.

buildSteps.title: Install the charging hardware
buildSteps.detail: Fit bidirectional chargers at homes, depots or car parks, each with its own protection and metering.

buildSteps.title: Connect the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Plug in and complete the handshake: the car and charger confirm voltage, current limits, state of charge and that the connector is locked.

buildSteps.title: Set driver permissions
buildSteps.detail: The owner specifies a minimum charge to keep and the hours the car may be used by the grid.

buildSteps.title: Register with an aggregator
buildSteps.detail: Software pools many vehicles so the fleet looks big enough for grid markets to accept.

buildSteps.title: Forecast and contract
buildSteps.detail: The aggregator predicts how much capacity will be plugged in and bids it into grid or balancing markets.

buildSteps.title: Dispatch a signal
buildSteps.detail: When the grid needs power, the aggregator sends a setpoint; chargers reverse the power flow.

buildSteps.title: Discharge and recharge
buildSteps.detail: Energy flows out of the batteries, then the cars are recharged within the time the driver allowed.

buildSteps.title: Settle and log
buildSteps.detail: Energy is metered and paid for, and the cycle count is recorded so battery wear can be compensated.

prerequisites.why: an agreed protocol is what lets any car and charger trade power safely; published standards now cover it.
most EVs and home chargers sold today are one-way only.
someone must measure and pay for the energy, or owners won't plug in.
local transformers and cables can be overloaded if many cars export at once.
rules have historically kept households and fleets out of frequency and capacity markets.

pathway.milestone: pilots and fleet depots where buses and vans provide grid services
pathway.unlocks: proof that aggregated vehicles can respond reliably.

pathway.milestone: standards-based home bidirectional charging on sale in volume
pathway.unlocks: millions of parked cars becoming a routine flexibility resource at peak times.

pathway.milestone: regulatory frameworks that let aggregators bid in national markets
pathway.unlocks: payment streams that make V2G hardware worth its extra cost to buyers.

pathway.milestone: V2G treated as normal grid infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: less need for peaking plants and grid batteries, and cheaper integration of solar and wind.
